title: Dynamic Attribute Access, Audit Logging, and Evidence Packaging Playbook
author: Aisha N. Ramos
body:
Summary
This playbook defines the guidance for integrating attribute-based access decisions (dynamic ABAC), the associated audit logging schema, evidence packaging for compliance reviews, and the incident triage steps that connect authorization events to forensic evidence. It is intended for security engineers, platform owners, and compliance reviewers implementing or operating Redwood Inference access controls for hosted, dedicated, and private offerings.

Goals and scope
- Provide a standard attribute and policy model for runtime authorization decisions.
- Ensure audit logs capture the inputs and outputs necessary to reproduce any authorization decision.
- Define retention, indexing, and evidence packaging requirements to support audits, legal holds, and incident investigations.
- Align secure-SDLC gating so changes to ABAC policies or logging code are controlled and traceable.

When to use this playbook
- Deploying or modifying dynamic attribute policies for tenant isolation, escalation controls, or administrative tooling.
- Onboarding a new customer with special data residency/retention constraints.
- Responding to incidents involving authorization failures or suspicious privilege escalations.

Definitions
- ABAC (Attribute-Based Access Control): authorization model that evaluates policies based on subject, resource, action, and environment attributes.
- Decision Record: the resolved allow/deny decision with policy id and evaluated attributes.
- Evidence Bundle: a packaged set of logs, policy versions, and configuration artifacts used for compliance reviews or investigations.

Design principles
1) Determinism: every decision must be reproducible from stored attributes, policy versions, and input context.
2) Minimal sensitive data in logs: never log raw secrets or full PII; store attribute references and hashed identifiers where required.
3) Linkability: audit entries must include stable identifiers for request, principal, policy-version, and runtime environment to enable correlation.
4) Tamper-evident storage: use write-once or append-only backed storage for high-sensitivity audit streams.

Attribute model (example)
- subject.id: stable internal principal id (uuid)
- subject.role: assigned roles (list)
- subject.clearance_level: integer 0-5
- resource.type: model|dataset|deployment|org-config
- resource.owner_org: org id
- action: read|write|invoke|admin|grant
- env.ip: requester IP (redacted/hashed in long-term logs)
- env.region: aws-us-west-2, gcp-europe-west1
- request.delegated_by: principal id when impersonation used

Policy metadata
Include in every policy: policy_id, version, author, created_at, change_request_id, signed_hash. Policies changed through the secure-SDLC (see "SDLC gate checklist" below).

Audit log schema (canonical JSON fields)
- event_timestamp: ISO8601
- request_id: uuid
- principal_id: subject.id
- principal_attrs: [subject.role, subject.clearance_level] (only attribute types; do not embed raw tokens)
- resource_id: resource identifier
- resource_type: resource.type
- action: action
- policy_id: policy_id@version
- decision: allow|deny|conditional
- decision_reasons: [short codes]
- evaluated_attributes_hash: sha256 of sorted key=value list (for reproducibility)
- policy_signed_hash: hex
- runtime_node: instance id or region tag
- retention_tier: tier_name (see retention table)
- signature: HMAC over the record when published to high-integrity streams

Retention tiers and indexing
| tier_name | data retained | retention_period | storage | index strategy |
| short-term | full audit JSON with request body refs | 90 days | hot index (elasticsearch) | tokenized on request_id, principal_id, policy_id |
| mid-term | canonical audit JSON (PII redacted) | 2 years | object store + warm index | indexed by principal_id, resource_type, action, decision |
| long-term | metadata-only and hashes (evidence tier) | 7 years or customer SLA | cold archive (WORM) | indexed by request_id and policy_signed_hash |

Note: for customers with data residency requirements, map retention_tier to the correct region-level bucket and record a residency_code in the audit entry.

Evidence Bundle creation (for audits & incidents)
1) Identify scope: list of request_ids, time window, affected principals/resources, relevant policy_ids.
2) Retrieve logs across tiers: pull short-term records where available, supplement with mid/long-term.
3) Collect supporting artifacts: policy source files, signed policy hash, deployment manifests, git change_request_ids, CI build artifacts, and change approvals.
4) Package: create a time-stamped archive with manifest.json listing all items and sha256 checksums.
5) Sign and record: store the bundle in the evidence catalog with chain-of-custody metadata (creator, date, retention).

Incident triage workflow (authorization-focused)
1) Triage: security oncall receives alert (e.g., repeated deny-to-allow flips, abnormal admin grants).
2) Fast gather: collect decision events for implicated request_ids and principals for +/- 24 hours.
3) Validation: confirm whether policy changes correlate by checking policy_signed_hash and git commit history.
4) Containment: if unauthorized grants are present, revoke related sessions and rotate delegation tokens.
5) Evidence bundle: generate evidence bundle and mark with legal hold if required.
6) Remediate: rollback faulty policy version or patch code path and validate in canary.
7) Post-incident: prepare a finding report with timeline, root cause, and preventive actions.

SDLC gate checklist for ABAC and audit changes
- All policy changes must be made via PRs in the policy repo and link a change_request_id.
- Automated unit/eval tests that assert decision vectors for canonical testcases.
- Peer review by at least one security engineer.
- CI pipeline must sign the policy artifact and publish the signed_hash.
- Deployment must be staged: dev -> canary (5% traffic) -> prod with rollback tags.
- Audit pipeline integration test: validate that a sample decision emits both short-term and mid-term records with correct indexed fields.

Query patterns and examples
- Find all denies for a principal in a day:
  SELECT * FROM audit_short_term WHERE principal_id = 'p-123' AND decision = 'deny' AND event_timestamp BETWEEN '2025-10-01' AND '2025-10-02';
- Reconstruct a decision: fetch audit entry by request_id, pull policy version by policy_signed_hash, and re-evaluate using saved evaluated_attributes_hash.

Operational SLOs and alerts
- Audit ingestion latency: 99th percentile < 45s for short-term stream.
- Policy sign/availability: 99.9% of active policy artifacts must be retrievable by policy_id@version.
- Evidence bundle build: end-to-end creation and cataloging < 4 hours for requests with < 10k events.
- Alerts: missing policy_signed_hash in >0.1% of events triggers high-priority investigation.

Ownership and contacts
- Policy engine owner: eng-platform/policy-service (oncall: @policy-oncall)
- Audit pipeline owner: eng-sre/audit-streams (oncall: @audit-oncall)
- Security response lead: security/incident-response (oncall: @sec-ir)

Appendix A — Redaction rules
- Never log secrets (API keys, tokens). Replace with <secret-redacted>.
- PII (email, phone) must be hashed with per-tenant salt; store salt metadata separately in vault.
- IP addresses: store as hashed_ip_short in mid/long-term.

Appendix B — Evidence manifest example (manifest.json)
{
  "bundle_id": "evid-20251102-0001",
  "created_by": "a.ramos",
  "time_window": "2025-10-31T00:00:00Z/2025-11-01T00:00:00Z",
  "items": ["audit_short/requests-20251031.json", "policies/policy-auth-v12.json", "git/commit-abc123.patch"],
  "checksums": {"audit_short/requests-20251031.json": "sha256:..."}
}
